methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $65M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
Vulcan Elements is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by John Maslin and Piotr Kulik, having raised $65M to date. The valuation analysis triangulates against a comp universe of 9 private robotics firms and 1 public comparable, including peers at similar and adjacent stages: Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, and Walden Robotics.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total capital raised as a proxy base and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A advancement, implies a valuation of $130M. Peer-median analysis across four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables yields a median valuation of $1.7B, with a range spanning $1.1B (Walden Robotics, Seed stage) to $2.0B (Generalist AI, Series B).

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $110M to $2.0B, with a median point of $915M. This wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty around two variables: (1) whether Vulcan's operational metrics and market position align more closely with seed-stage peers or with advanced Series B companies commanding billion-plus valuations, and (2) the stage-progression methodology's sensitivity to assumed step-up multiples, which may not reflect sector-specific capital efficiency norms. The peer-median implied value suggests market comparables substantially exceed the stage-progression floor, indicating investor pricing power conditional on execution and competitive positioning within the robotics sector.
